description:
Look a Latgalian word up on Wiktionary and return its senses plus full
declension/conjugation tables — attested content, not invented. Any form of
the word works; an inflected query is resolved to its lemma automatically
via previously cached paradigms and the result notes the resolution. With
search_language='eng' the query is an English word instead: the result
lists its per-sense Latgalian equivalents (the translations block) plus
their expanded entries. Returns Markdown plus the same result as
structuredContent matching the declared outputSchema.

Results are cached server-side; first-time queries reach the live upstream
politely and calls are rate limited — on a rate-limit error, wait a few
seconds and retry. Content is from en.wiktionary.org (CC BY-SA 4.0 —
attribute and share alike if republished).

SearchLanguage.description:
The query language. ``ltg`` looks a Latgalian word up directly (any of its
forms — an inflected query resolves via cached paradigms). ``eng`` searches in
reverse: the English Wiktionary page for the query word lists per-sense
Latgalian translations, and each distinct lemma is then looked up normally.
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

include_forms.description: When true (default), each match's full declension/conjugation table is returned INLINE — usable cases/tenses in ONE call, no follow-up latgalian_get_inflections. Set false for a cheap screen of which entries exist. Bounded by a per-search cap — use max_forms to adjust per call. For eng queries this governs the expanded Latgalian entries; the per-sense translations list itself is always returned.
include_forms.title: Include Forms

max_forms.description: Optional override for how many inflection tables to expand this call (0–12). On an uncached query each table is one politely paced upstream fetch, so high values on cold queries are slow. Omit for the server default.
max_forms.title: Max Forms

query.description: The word to look up, in the language search_language names. Latgalian (default): a SINGLE Latgalian word, any form — an inflected form ('akmiņa') is resolved to its lemma ('akmiņs') automatically via cached paradigms, and the result says so; diacritics are optional once a paradigm is cached ('akmins' finds 'akmiņs'). English (search_language='eng'): the English word whose Latgalian equivalents you want — multiword entries like 'apple tree' work.
query.title: Query

search_language.description: Language the query word is in: 'ltg' (default) looks the Latgalian word up directly; 'eng' finds the Latgalian equivalents of an English word (per-sense, from Wiktionary's translation tables) and returns their full entries. Glosses are in English either way.

Entry.description:
One Latgalian entry on the page: the headword (page title) with one
part-of-speech section's senses.
Entry.title: Entry

InflectionHandle.description:
A structured anchor for fetching a full paradigm: feed ``entry_id`` (the page
title) + ``word_class`` (the POS section) to ``latgalian_get_inflections`` — or
ask ``search`` to include the table inline (``forms``).

entry_id.description: Wiktionary page title — the lemma itself.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

forms.description: The full paradigm, populated when a search is asked to include forms. None when not requested or beyond the cap.
forms.title: Forms

InflectionHandle.title: InflectionHandle

LatgalianNominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/etc.: case key → {singular, plural}.

Noun tables give the bare case ('nominative', 'genitive', … — the seven
Latgalian cases), with no definiteness. Adjective tables come as a family:
the state (indefinite/definite, from the table's NavHead) prefixes the key and
the gender (masculine/feminine, from the header row) suffixes it —
'indefinite nominative masculine', 'definite locative feminine'.
``category`` discriminates this from the verbal and not-found shapes — switch
on it before reading the body.

cases.description: Case key (lower-case: 'nominative', 'genitive', …; nouns use the bare case; adjectives prefix the state — 'indefinite nominative' — and suffix the gender — 'indefinite nominative masculine') → its singular/plural forms, in table order.
cases.title: Cases

LatgalianNumberForms.description:
A declension cell: the two number forms of one case key. Forms are verbatim
Latgalian; alternates stay comma-separated as Wiktionary renders them. A number
the table doesn't give (defective paradigms) is an empty string.
LatgalianNumberForms.title: LatgalianNumberForms

LatgalianVerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way Wiktionary's tables are: finite cells
keyed by mood (and, for the indicative, tense) → person-or-number → form, plus
the non-finite forms (infinitive, supine, verbal noun, converb, debitive and
the participles). The negative conjugation renders as its own table and its keys
carry a 'negative ' prefix; positive keys are bare.

finite.description: Mood key (lower-case: 'indicative present', 'indicative past', 'indicative future', 'subjunctive', 'imperative'; the negative table's keys are prefixed — 'negative indicative past') → person or number ('first singular' … 'third plural'; the imperative uses bare 'singular'/'plural') → the form. Alternates are comma-separated; an em-dash cell (no such form) is omitted.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite form ('infinitive', 'supine', 'verbal noun', 'converb', 'debitive', and the participles keyed by tense and voice — 'past active participle', 'present passive participle'; negative-prefixed for that table) → {'form': <the form>}.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite
